title: Vernal's volunteer-run haunted hotel hosts its final Halloween before demolition

content:
VERNAL, Utah (KUTV) — A volunteer-run haunted hotel in eastern Utah will host its final night on Halloween after eight years of spooky exhibits and an estimated $600,000 raised for local charities.

The popular Hotel Vernal Haunt is closing its doors after this season, as the deteriorating old hotel is set for demolition come April.

The hotel once served as a popular spot for tourists and community events in the mid-1900s, but became run down, closing its doors in 1991. It sat mostly empty for decades until Quinn Bennion and Megan Carroll-Munoz had an idea.

They formed a committee to open a haunted attraction in the aging hotel, using the old building to their advantage.

"It's a wonderful venue for the Hotel Haunt," Bennion said. "It fits perfectly, right? It already has a haunted vibe to it, and we're great that it looks old and looks creepy."

Photos from the 2023 Hotel Vernal Haunt charity fundraiser taken on Thursday, Oct. 26, 2023, in Vernal, Utah. (Photo: Hotel Vernal Haunt)

The Haunt has more than 200 volunteers and 100 sponsors. With volunteers running the hotel and sponsors paying for expenses, all the ticket sales go to local nonprofits.

Organizers estimate that they've raised about $600,000 for local nonprofits since they first reopened the old hotel's doors in 2018.

"One hundred percent of the ticket sales go to the charities. So we feel very blessed that we are able to do that, and making sure that it goes back to the community and stays here as well," Carroll-Munoz said.

When the Haunt first opened, Bennion said downtown Vernal was "quiet" with lots of storefront vacancies and only a few open restaurants. He said one of their main priorities with the Halloween attraction was to get people to come to Main Street, and it worked.

On October weekends, hundreds of people will wait their turn for the Hotel Haunt, with the lines wrapping around the block. The small town of Vernal has a population of under 11,000 people, and the hotel drew 1,000 visitors on Friday alone.

Bennion said that not all the visitors are from the area, with some traveling from the Wasatch Front, Colorado or Wyoming to go through the hotel.

Photos from the 2023 Hotel Vernal Haunt charity fundraiser taken on Thursday, Oct. 26, 2023, in Vernal, Utah. (Photo: Hotel Vernal Haunt)

While the hotel has helped bring energy to downtown, it has helped community members on a more personal level as well. Carroll-Munoz said some of the young actors have expressed that the Haunt has helped them find a safe place in the community where they feel they belong.

"They may not belong to the cheerleaders, the football team, but we go and put a mask on them and suddenly they are completely in their element," she said. "It has given them a place of belonging and where they're welcomed."

Organizers always knew the hotel had an expiration date, as there were no investments being made in the building. They were told a couple of years back that the hotel would be demolished and turned into a community plaza.

Photos from the 2026 Hotel Vernal Haunt in Vernal, Utah, taken on Oct. 17, 2026. (Credit: Geoff Liesik)

Bennion and Carroll-Munoz called the end of the Hotel Haunt "bittersweet," saying that it's hard to end something that has forged so many connections within the community. But at the same time, they are looking forward to having free time again, and taking a nap.

"I keep telling my husband that we'll go on our first vacation in the fall," Carroll-Munoz said. "We've all sacrificed quite a bit in order to make sure that the Haunt happens with a lot of professionalism and a lot of creativity."

It's the end of a chapter for the community's haunted hotel, but the memories of the Haunt, and the money donated to charities, will continue to impact the Uintah Basin community long after the hotel is torn down.

"We've had other towns that have come and walked through the hotel and they're like, 'We could never get our town to do something like that.' And just to know that we have helped to create something where everybody has come together, it's our own little Hallmark," Carroll-Munoz said.

"Yeah, Halloween Hallmark," Bennion added.
